network.title: Network
network.subtitle: All network settings in one place — mode, internet source, Wi-Fi and ports, changeable at any time.
network.mode_router_desc: Internet arrives over a cable or a modem; the device hands it out over Wi-Fi and wired ports.
network.mode_extender_desc: The device joins an existing Wi-Fi network and re-broadcasts its own.
network.wan_ethernet_desc: Cable from your ISP or router
network.no_cable: No cable plugged into any port.
network.modem_none: No modem detected. Plug in a USB modem with a SIM.
network.ap_psk_help: 8–63 characters. Empty means an open network (not recommended).
network.band_help: One band at a time — the Pi's built-in Wi-Fi can't run 2.4 and 5 GHz together (that needs a second adapter).
network.ports_help: Tick the wired ports that should hand out internet. They are bridged with Wi-Fi into one network.
network.lan_help: The LAN subnet and DHCP address range. Change only if you know why.
network.reapply_warn: Applying rebuilds the network — Wi-Fi clients briefly reconnect. If the new config fails to bring the AP up, the change is rolled back automatically.

profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.subtitle: Schedules and DNS filters that get assigned to devices
profiles.empty_help: Assign a profile to a device from its detail page to make the schedule and filter take effect.
profiles.id_help: Lowercase letters, digits, hyphen. Used in URLs; cannot be changed after creation.
profiles.description_placeholder: What this profile does (shown on the device page)
profiles.schedule_help: When devices on this profile lose internet. LAN and admin UI keep working.
profiles.blocklists_help: Comma-separated blocklist names (e.g. ads, trackers). The lists themselves arrive in M11.
profiles.safesearch_help: Locks Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo and YouTube into their safe/restricted modes for devices on this profile.
profiles.builtin_locked: Built-in profile — schedule and filters editable, but cannot be deleted.
profiles.err_id_format: Lowercase letters, digits, dot, hyphen, underscore (1-64)

device.profile_help: Applies the schedule and DNS filter to this device.

devices.title: Devices
devices.subtitle: Every device that has ever joined this network
devices.empty_help: Devices will appear here once they connect to the Wi-Fi and get a DHCP lease.
devices.bw_help: Live traffic from netfilter conntrack — counters reset on knotd restart, smoothed over 2-second samples.
devices.stale_help: Device hasn't answered ARP for over 30 days. Likely won't reconnect with this MAC (iOS/Android rotate private MACs). Safe to remove via "Forget device".
devices.display_name_help: Only visible to you in this admin UI. The device itself doesn't see it.
devices.wake_help: Wired devices with WoL enabled in BIOS can be powered on from here — knotd sends a magic packet to the LAN broadcast. The device should appear online within 30 seconds.
devices.wake_sent: Magic packet sent. If WoL is enabled in BIOS, the device will wake within 30 seconds.
devices.quarantine_help: New devices get no internet until you approve them. Current devices are approved automatically.
devices.landing_help: A blocked device sees an explanatory page (paused / awaiting approval / blocked) on any site it opens. Pops up automatically.
devices.forget_help: Removes the entry from the list. Useful for duplicates created by iOS/Android private-MAC randomization, where one phone shows up under several MACs over time. If the same MAC reconnects, the entry comes back automatically.
devices.forget_online_error: Device is online — wait for it to disconnect first

auth.not_configured: Device hasn't been set up yet

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.wan_subtitle_modem: Internet connection over the cellular modem

setup.detect_timeout: Hardware probe took too long. You can continue and try again later, or refresh.

welcome.title: Hi there! 👋
welcome.subtitle: Welcome to KnotOS — your home router. Let's set it up together. Takes about 3–5 minutes.

hw.title: What I see
hw.subtitle: Quick look at what hardware is here. Nothing's been changed yet.
hw.no_eth: No Ethernet adapter detected. KnotOS will run as a Wi-Fi extender — that's fine.
hw.rec_router_ready: Everything's set up for full router mode — Internet via cable, Wi-Fi for your devices.
hw.rec_router_no_cable: Plug an Ethernet cable in to use full router mode. Without one, you can still set up Wi-Fi extender mode.
hw.rec_extender_only: We'll set this up as a Wi-Fi extender — joins your existing network and broadcasts its own.
hw.cable_detected: Ethernet cable detected — you can switch to router mode now.
hw.power_hint_title: If the AP drops when you plug the cable in
hw.power_hint_body: On Pi Zero 2W, USB-Ethernet adapters can briefly brown out the SoC and reset the Wi-Fi chip. Use a 5V/3A power supply or a powered USB hub. The AP comes back on its own; just wait 10–15 seconds.

role.title: What's the job?
role.subtitle: KnotOS can be either a full router (Internet → KnotOS → Wi-Fi for everyone) or a repeater (extends an existing network).
role.router_desc: Wired or cellular internet in, Wi-Fi out. Best when KnotOS replaces the main router.
role.extender_desc: Joins your existing Wi-Fi and rebroadcasts it. Better signal in distant rooms, no cable needed.
role.no_router_reason: Need an Ethernet adapter for router mode — none detected.
role.cable_warning: No cable detected — connect Ethernet, or pick a cellular modem on the next step.
role.help_a1: Have you got an Ethernet cable from your ISP / modem? → Full router.
role.help_a2: Already have a Wi-Fi router and want better coverage upstairs? → Wi-Fi extender.
role.help_a3: Want every device on your LAN to use a VPN or DNS filter? → Full router gives you the most control.

conn.router_subtitle: Pick which port goes to your modem / ISP. Most setups: just DHCP and you're done.
conn.extender_subtitle: The network KnotOS will join. Stronger signal = faster speeds for your devices.
conn.wan_type_label: How does this router get internet?
conn.wan_modem_desc: Share internet from a USB SIM modem
conn.modem_none: No modem detected yet. Plug in a USB LTE modem — you can still finish setup and it'll connect once present.
conn.no_cable: No Ethernet cable plugged in. Connect one and step back / forward to refresh.
conn.lan_ports_help: Tick the ports that should hand out internet over a cable. They are bridged with Wi-Fi into one network.
conn.pppoe_desc: If your ISP gave you a username and password
conn.pppoe_help: Your ISP put these in your contract. If unsure — call them and ask.
conn.pppoe_wip: PPPoE is still in development — choose DHCP
conn.no_networks: No networks found nearby. Make sure your home Wi-Fi is on and you're in range.

wifi.title: Your Wi-Fi network
wifi.subtitle: What name and password should your devices use to connect.
wifi.ssid_help: What people see when they pick a network. Up to 32 characters; emoji and spaces are fine.
wifi.psk_help: Min 8 characters. Use a memorable phrase or a passphrase from your password manager.
wifi.pw_ok: OK — but a few more characters wouldn't hurt
wifi.band_note: One band at a time. 5 GHz is faster and cleaner but shorter range.
wifi.channel_help: 1, 6, 11 are the cleanest in most homes. «Auto» picks based on a scan at startup.
wifi.qr_help: Phones can connect by scanning this with their camera
wifi.qr_pending: Fill in name + password to see the QR

admin.title: Admin access
admin.subtitle: How you'll get into KnotOS to manage it later.
admin.device_name_help: Hostname for KnotOS. You'll see «{name}.local» in your phone's browser.
admin.country_help: Two-letter code (RU, US, DE). Sets the legal Wi-Fi channels.
admin.password_help: This is for KnotOS web admin — NOT your Wi-Fi password. Keep them different.
admin.tg_help: Get notifications and control KnotOS from Telegram. You can do this later from System → Notifications.

review.title: All set?
review.subtitle: Quick check before we apply. Everything reversible if it doesn't work.
review.line_tg: Telegram bot will be ready to link after first login
review.rollback_promise: If something goes wrong within 30 seconds — KnotOS rolls back automatically. No risk.

apply.title: Setting up…
apply.subtitle: Hang tight, this takes a few seconds.
apply.failed_rolled_back: We rolled back to the previous state — your KnotOS is back where it was. Try again with adjusted settings.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.subtitle: Optional features that extend KnotOS
plugins.empty_help: Plugins live under /usr/lib/knot/plugins/. Restart knotd after installing one to discover it.
plugins.spec_error: The plugin returned an invalid UI.
plugins.runtime_stopped_help: Enable the plugin on the manage page to start its process.
plugins.uninstall_confirm: Remove the plugin "{name}" from the device?
plugins.store_subtitle: Catalog from GitHub. Official plugins are signed with the release key and install directly; third-party ones need confirmation.
plugins.store_empty: Every available plugin is already installed.
plugins.confirm_body: "{name}" is not signed by a trusted key. It runs as a separate process on your router with access to the host API. Only install from a source you trust. Continue?
plugins.v01_note: Enabled plugins run as separate processes and talk to the router through the host API, scoped by the permissions in their manifest.

system.title: System
system.subtitle: Manage your device
system.shutdown_confirm: Shut down? You'll need physical access to power it back on.
system.factory_reset_warn: Wipes settings and re-runs the setup wizard. Current passwords and Wi-Fi configs will be lost.
system.update_subtitle: Upload a new knotd binary to update without re-flashing
system.update_sig_hint: Images built with a release key require an Ed25519 .sig file. Sign the binary with your rescue key via knot-sign and attach the .sig here.

security.subtitle: Local root certificate that signs the admin UI's TLS cert. Install it on your devices once and the browser will stop warning about an "unsafe connection".
security.regenerate_confirm: Re-issue the leaf? The root stays the same, so trust copies installed on your devices remain valid. The browser may ask you to reconnect right after.
security.install_help: On iOS and macOS you also need to enable the root in Trusted Root Certificates (Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings). On Android, install through Settings → Security → Advanced → Encryption & credentials → Install from SD card.

protection.title: Protection
protection.subtitle: DNS-level ad and tracker blocking, scoped per device and profile
protection.refresh_queued: Blocklist refresh started in the background
protection.top_blocked_empty: Nothing has been blocked yet — browse a bit and stats will appear here.
protection.sources_empty: Lists haven't loaded yet. They'll appear within a minute of startup, or hit "Refresh lists".
protection.upstream_subtitle: Where knotd forwards queries that aren't blocked. DoH hides domain names from your ISP and from on-path censoring middleboxes.
protection.upstream_mode_udp_help: Plain DNS over UDP/53. Fast, but your ISP sees every query in cleartext.
protection.upstream_mode_doh_help: RFC 8484: queries ride a TLS tunnel to /dns-query. The ISP sees only the TLS handshake to Cloudflare/Quad9.
protection.upstream_list_help_udp: One per line as host:port. Empty falls back to Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 + Google 8.8.8.8.
protection.upstream_list_help_doh: Full https:// URLs ending in /dns-query. Empty falls back to Cloudflare + Quad9.
protection.queries_empty: No queries yet. As devices resolve domains, they'll show up here.
protection.disabled_help: Protection turns on once the device leaves setup mode and enters Wi-Fi extender role. Come back here once setup is finished.

updates.subtitle: Fetch a fresh knotd binary from GitHub Releases, verified with an Ed25519 signature. Atomic replace, automatic service restart.
updates.signing_off: This build was compiled without a release key — signature checks are off. Don't use in production.
updates.apply_confirm: Install version {version}? The binary will be downloaded, signature-verified, atomically replaced, and knotd restarted. Your session survives.
updates.manual_help: Developer-only: uploads a locally-built knotd without signature verification. For normal updates, use the /system/update/apply path above.
updates.disabled: Auto-update is disabled in this build (no signing key, or dev mode).
updates.error_timeout: GitHub did not respond in time. Check the device's internet and try again.
updates.error_github: Could not reach GitHub. Make sure the Pi has internet access.

rescue.subtitle: Per-device Ed25519 key. A knotd binary signed by this key is accepted even if the upstream release key has been compromised. The private half is shown exactly once — save it somewhere safe.
rescue.reveal_confirm: Reveal the private key? This is irreversible — after the click the key is wiped from the device, only your copy remains. If you lose it you'll need to re-flash to generate a new one.
rescue.warning_one_shot: Once you click, the private key disappears from the device forever. Save it immediately.
rescue.already_revealed_help: The private key has been delivered. Only the public half remains here. To regenerate, delete /etc/knot/rescue.json and restart knotd.
rescue.error_already_revealed: Private key was already revealed earlier.

vpn.title: WireGuard server
vpn.subtitle: WireGuard road-warrior — reach your home LAN from anywhere by scanning a QR. Per-peer profiles work the same as on the LAN: ad-block + schedules travel with you.
vpn.endpoint_help: Either a DDNS hostname (no-ip, Cloudflare, duckdns) or a public IP. Whatever you set ends up in every peer's client config — no endpoint, no incoming connections.
vpn.peers_empty: No peers yet. Click "Add peer" to issue a config for your phone / laptop.
vpn.full_tunnel_help: On: everything from the peer goes through home (more private, slower on the road). Off: only LAN-bound traffic uses the VPN.
vpn.remove_confirm: Remove peer "{name}"? Its old QR will stop working.
vpn.delivery_help: Open the WireGuard app on the peer device, tap "+" → "Scan from QR code" and point the camera at the screen. Tunnel is up in a second.
vpn.delivery_warning: The private key is shown ONCE. Close this dialog and it's gone forever. If lost, delete the peer and create a new one.
vpn.disabled: VPN endpoints are disabled in this build.

guests.title: Guest network
guests.subtitle: Time-limited Wi-Fi with a one-time password and QR. Guests reach the internet but are walled off from your main LAN.
guests.empty_help: Spin up a temporary guest network — knotd generates the password and draws a QR. Your guest scans it with their phone camera and connects in one tap. The network disappears on its own when the timer runs out.
guests.ssid_help: Up to 32 characters. Empty defaults to your main SSID + «-guest».
guests.revoke_confirm: Close the guest network right now? Connected guests will lose Wi-Fi instantly.
guests.isolation_help: Guests can't see your main LAN devices — internet only. Separate subnet, separate DHCP scope, drop on forwarding between guest and LAN.
guests.disabled: Guest network requires Wi-Fi router mode on Pi 4/5 with USB Ethernet, or a Zero 2W with a multi-BSS-capable Wi-Fi driver.

notify.subtitle: The bot pushes alerts on important events and accepts commands with inline keyboards — control your router right from Telegram.
notify.step1_botfather: Create a bot: message @BotFather → /newbot → name → @username. You'll get a token like 1234567890:ABC...
notify.step1_paste: Paste the token below and save. knotd verifies it via getMe and starts the bot loop.
notify.mtproto_help: By default the bot uses the HTTP Bot API (api.telegram.org), which is blocked in some regions. Enter an app_id + app_hash from my.telegram.org and the bot connects over MTProto through the local Telegram proxy instead.
notify.mtproto_no_proxy: Enable the Telegram proxy on the Censorship bypass page so the bot can reach Telegram through it.
notify.pin_help: Open the bot, press /start, send this code. Expires in {sec}s.
notify.unlink_confirm: Unlink this chat? The bot will stop accepting commands and stop sending notifications there.

channels.subtitle: Scan the airwaves and recommend which of channels 1/6/11 is least crowded by neighbouring APs. Wi-Fi router mode only — extender mode pins the channel to the upstream.
channels.apply_help: The AP will restart, connected clients will drop briefly and reconnect on their own.
channels.already_optimal: Already on the optimal channel per the latest scan.

routing.title: VPN
routing.subtitle: Send each device through any VPN server you've subscribed to — like Happ, but for your whole LAN. Paste a subscription URL or a single vless:// share link, and assign servers to profiles.
routing.empty_help: Paste your provider's subscription URL or drop a single vless://, vmess://, trojan:// or ss:// link to get started.
routing.manual_help: One-off share links you pasted directly. They won't update automatically — re-paste to refresh.
routing.add_ua_help: Some providers gate quota info on a known UA. Leave empty to use knotd's default.
routing.add_uri_help: The link goes into «Manual entries» and is parsed locally — no upstream call.
routing.server_direct_help: Traffic from this profile leaves your normal WAN, no VPN.
routing.split_help: Route only specific domains through the tunnel; everything else stays direct.
routing.split_modal_help: Only traffic to these domains (and their subdomains) goes through the tunnel. Everything else from devices on this profile stays direct.
routing.split_empty_help: One domain per line, e.g. youtube.com. Leave empty to tunnel the whole device.
routing.profiles_help: Each profile chooses one outbound. Devices inherit that decision via their profile assignment.
routing.devices_help: Live status of every known device. Status «kill» means the requested server is gone — fix it by re-fetching the subscription or picking another server.
routing.status_kill_help: The server this profile asks for is missing from any subscription. Traffic is dropped, not leaked.
routing.missing_outbounds: {count, plural, one {# server is missing} other {# servers are missing}}
routing.remove_subscription_confirm: Remove subscription "{name}"? Profiles routing through its servers will switch to kill-switch.
routing.disabled: Subscription endpoints are disabled in this build.

portforward.title: Port forwarding
portforward.subtitle: Let traffic from the internet reach a device on your LAN — for game servers, NAS, cameras and the like.
portforward.not_router: Port forwarding only takes effect in router mode (the extender has no WAN of its own). Rules are saved but won't be active.
portforward.empty: No port forwards yet. Add one below.
portforward.security_note: Forwarded ports are reachable from the internet. Only forward services you trust and keep them patched.
portforward.disabled: Port-forward endpoints are disabled in this build.

zapret.title: Censorship bypass
zapret.subtitle: Reach blocked services without a full VPN: DPI bypass (nfqws) for YouTube/Discord, and a local proxy for Telegram.
zapret.tg_subtitle: A local MTProto proxy on the router: phones on your network reach Telegram through the bypass. Tunnels to Telegram's servers over WebSocket.
zapret.tg_enable_help: Runs an MTProto proxy on the router. Then add it to Telegram via the link below.
zapret.tg_will_download: The proxy binary is downloaded the first time you enable it.
zapret.tg_link_help: Open this link on a phone (on your Wi-Fi) — Telegram will offer to connect the proxy. Or copy and send it to yourself.
zapret.tg_not_router: The proxy only works in full-router mode.
zapret.not_router: Zapret only works in router mode (it acts on traffic leaving the WAN). Settings are saved but won't be active in extender mode.
zapret.enable_help: Starts the nfqws engine and its nftables hook for the domain lists below.
zapret.will_download: nfqws isn't on this device yet — it will be downloaded and verified (~125 KB) the first time you enable it.
zapret.strategy_help: DPI behaviour differs per ISP. If one strategy doesn't break through, save and try the next — exactly like Flowseal's presets.
zapret.autotune_help: Test every preset against YouTube/Discord and pick the one that works.
zapret.autotune_running: Trying each strategy against YouTube/Discord test hosts — this takes up to a minute. The connection may blip while it switches.
zapret.autotune_winner: Picked the best strategy (highlighted below) and enabled it.
zapret.autotune_not_needed: The test hosts already work without a bypass — you probably don't need Zapret on this connection.
zapret.autotune_none: No strategy got through the DPI here. The bypass was left off. Try a custom strategy, refresh from Flowseal, or this network may block these hosts outright rather than throttle them.
zapret.custom_help: Paste a raw nfqws argument string (e.g. adapted from a Flowseal .bat). Overrides the preset.
zapret.custom_placeholder_help: {LISTS} and {BIN} expand to the on-disk lists/ and bin/ directories. Profiles are separated by --new.
zapret.lists_help: Domain lists AND the strategy presets are pulled live from the upstream Flowseal repo and stored on disk — so they stay current without a firmware update. The presets above are the real Flowseal strategies, converted to nfqws.
zapret.tip: Tip: enable, pick General, save — then test YouTube/Discord. No luck? Switch to ALT/ALT2 and save again. The lists only cover YouTube + Discord, so the rest of your traffic is untouched.
zapret.disabled: Zapret endpoints are disabled in this build.

modem.title: Cellular modem (SIM)
modem.subtitle: Share internet from a USB LTE/4G modem — as the main WAN or a failover.
modem.experimental: Experimental: cellular WAN via ModemManager. Behavior may vary between modems.
modem.not_router: A cellular modem can only be the WAN in full-router mode (the extender uses a Wi-Fi uplink).
modem.none_help: Plug in a USB LTE modem. QMI/MBIM sticks (Quectel, Sierra) are driven via ModemManager; HiLink dongles that appear as a network card can instead be used as a normal DHCP WAN.
modem.pin_required: The SIM is PIN-locked — enter the PIN below and save.
modem.sim_slot_help: This modem exposes more than one SIM slot. Switching resets the modem and reconnects on the selected SIM.
modem.data_limit_help: 0 = no cap. Just used to show the usage bar and warn when reached.
modem.cycle_reset_day_help: Day of month (1–28) the usage counter resets, matching your plan.
modem.network_mode_help: Lock the modem to a generation. "4G" (LTE-only) is often steadier with an external MIMO antenna. Changing it briefly drops the connection.
modem.bands_help: Lock to specific RF bands, or leave all selected for automatic. Advanced — only touch if you know which band your cell uses.
modem.ussd_help: Run a carrier code, e.g. *100# to check a prepaid balance.
modem.usage_none: No usage recorded yet — it appears once the modem carries traffic.
modem.network_none: This modem doesn't report selectable network modes.
modem.as_wan: Use the modem as the internet uplink (WAN)
modem.as_wan_help: Routes all internet traffic through the cellular modem instead of Ethernet.
modem.apn_help: Carrier access point. Most SIMs auto-configure — leave blank to try the default, or enter e.g. "internet".
modem.pin_help: Only if your SIM asks for a PIN. Leave blank to keep the current one.
modem.switch_warning: Switching the WAN to the modem reconfigures the uplink — wired internet stops being used. Make sure the modem + SIM are ready.
modem.disabled: Modem endpoints are disabled in this build.

messages.title: Messages
messages.subtitle: SMS through the cellular modem.
messages.no_modem: No cellular modem detected. Messages are available when a modem is present.
messages.pick: Pick a conversation, or start a new one.
